title: COVID-19 Pandemic Causes Shortest-Ever US Recession With Record GDP Plunge
reason: Confirmed on all material points. NBER's Business Cycle Dating Committee officially announced (July 19, 2021) that the US recession lasted from February 2020 to April 2020 — just two months, the shortest recession in US history since NBER records began (prior shortest was six months, in 1980). This was despite it being one of the deepest recessions on record, justified by the unprecedented magnitude/breadth of the employment and production collapse. BEA's official GDP releases confirm the growth figures exactly as described: real GDP fell at a 31.4% annualized rate in Q2 2020 (this is the BEA's final/"third estimate," released Dec. 2020 — earlier advance/second estimates had been -32.9%/-31.7%, converging to -31.4%), then rebounded at a 33.4% annualized rate in Q3 2020 (also the BEA's final "third estimate" of Dec. 22, 2020; advance was 33.1%). Both the recession dating rationale and the exact GDP percentages in the event description match official NBER and BEA sources precisely.

verifications.reason: NBER's Business Cycle Dating Committee (announced July 19, 2021) officially dated a peak in February 2020 and trough in April 2020 — a two-month recession, the shortest on record (prior shortest was six months in 1980). BEA data independently confirms real GDP fell at a 31.4% annualized rate in Q2 2020 (third/final estimate) and rebounded at 33.4% annualized in Q3 2020 (third estimate) — both figures exactly as described. All material details (country=US, year=2020, dates, magnitudes, dating rationale) check out against authoritative primary sources (NBER, BEA).
